- session_log_deletion_manifest.csv (redacted, shows deletion timestamps + job ids)
- vertex_hold_workflow_diagram.png (how hold requests flow through our ops)

A few clarifying bullets about the hold process:
- Initiation: authenticated request via your account owner + security contact OR HubSpot security form tied to your org id.
- Authorization: Security Ops triages within 4 hours; short holds (<=14 days) auto-apply after triage. Longer holds require PR approval from Security Lead and a written justification; extensions are logged and require weekly review.
- Evidence on release: when a hold is released we run the same deletion pipeline and produce a deletion manifest (CSV) and a signed attestation (PDF) that lists affected shard ids, deletion job ids, and UTC timestamps.
- Contract note: long-term holds (>90 days) are considered an exception and will be documented as a retained scope in an addendum.

If you want, Priyom from our engineering team can join a call to show the manifest schema and demo a redaction-proof hash that we include in the attestation. Proposed times: Tue 2028-07-05 10:00am PDT or Wed 2028-07-06 2:00pm PDT.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Security Ops Manager, Redwood Inference

Elena, Stephanie — quick technical notes to prep for the call:

- Manifest schema: we include a salted SHA256 field (example: sha256(salt || session_id)) and we retain the salt in a HSM-backed key ring for 30 days after deletion in order to support audit verification. The playbook explains the rotation policy.
- Attestation: signed with our platform key via AWS KMS; the PDF includes a manifest hash and list of shard ids.
- SLA/notifications: when a hold is applied we send an automated notice to the customer's security contact within 2 hours; extensions produce an update email with justification and expected release date.

We'll add the salt-management reference and the legal escalation lane to the diagram before the call. Sending calendar invite now for Tue 2028-07-05 10:00am PDT.
